messages:
ajay: Quick proposal for telemetry/inspect rollout — want feedback. TL;DR: per-route opt-in debug traces, sample-only capture, per-tenant HMAC pseudonyms, ephemeral inspect tokens (24h TTL), console request flow + audit records. Need input on quotas, console UX, and PII redaction :eyes:
sophie: Sounds good. Two quick q's: (1) where do raw traces live for canary? (2) how do we surface cost impact to the user in the console?
marco: We must avoid storing PII. My suggestion: never store raw identifiers long-term. Hash sensitive fields with tenant-specific salt via KMS-backed HMAC. Truncate HMAC to 128 bits for joins but not reversible. Also add rate-limited access to any raw artifacts. :lock:
ajay: Agree. Implementation sketch: store only hashed ids + metadata for normal sampling. For canary we allow a very small number of raw captures (encrypted at rest, short TTL) behind a manual unmask process that requires SRE + legal signoff.
sophie: Console UX idea: "Request debug" button -> modal with TTL, justification text, list of approvers, and estimated token/cost delta. Show approval status and audit link. Default state DENIED for non-admins.
zara: Ops concerns: quotas. Propose per-tenant knobs: inspect-samples-per-day, inspect-token-concurrent, and a global circuit-breaker that disables inspect for tenant when spend > threshold. Also an alert channel for billing spikes. :warning:
ajay: Sampling approach: deterministic route-weighted sampler with sticky short-lived inspect ids. Example config:
```
sampler:
  strategy: route-weighted
  seed: hmac(tenant_id, route)
  inspect_rate: 0.001  # 0.1%
  sticky_ttl: 1h
```
Expose effective sample rate on per-route page so teams see cost/latency tradeoffs.
marco: Note on embeddings: embeddings can leak PII. Store only vectors + hashed provenance (no raw text). If someone requests raw input for debug, run redaction heuristics first (emails, cc numbers, SSNs), then route to manual review. Never auto-serve raw embeddings.
sophie: For canaries, we could create a sandbox view where product/pm can see raw for a bounded window (by role), but require explicit checkbox acknowledging risk.
devex-bot: deploy-canary: created topic telemetry-inspect-v2 (canary) — tag=telemetry-inspect-v2 :robot_face:
zara: Rollback story: automatic disable if unmask usage or cost spikes. Trigger: if (inspect_token_count * avg_token_cost) > tenant_threshold -> auto-disable inspect tokens + create incident + notify account team.
ajay: We'll add a circuit-breaker + a short SLA for appeals. Also implement an "inspect-grace" where teams can request emergency unmask with multi-party approval via console.
marco: Audit requirements: every unmask/approve event must emit a signed audit record (no payload) containing: HMAC_trace_id, approver, justification, timestamp, TTL, reason. Store audit records for 7 years (compliance).
sophie: Storage for raw canary captures: s3 encrypted with tenant KMS, lifecycle 7 days, access only via jumpbox and ephemeral creds. Put a flag in console for who accessed and when.
zara: Metrics to add: unmask_request_rate, unmask_approval_latency, sample_rate_by_route, redaction_failure_rate, inspect_cost_estimate. Those should be on ops dashboard and route-level page.
ajay: Next steps: I'll draft an RFC with: console mockups, quota knobs, pseudonymization API, sample code, and a small migration plan. Target: mini-canary in 2 weeks, broader rollout after legal + security signoff. Can folks ack or drop comments here?
marco: Ack, will add privacy review checklist to RFC.
sophie: Ack — I'll mock the modal and the approval workflow.
zara: Ack — will wire alerts + circuit-breaker metrics.
oncall-bot: incident-monitor: created alert channel #inspect-usage-alerts for tenant spikes.
ajay: Thanks — putting RFC on my plate. If anyone has objections about the HMAC/truncation approach speak now, otherwise I'll start writing. :thumbsup:
